kind: PRODUCT fix for three of phase 12's six confirmed MAJORs, all on the python side and all downstream of ONE structural fact the gate's adjudicator named: no test in either leg executes scripts/serve.py's main(). The seams below main() are well tested and the call sites above them are pinned only by source-text greps, so every defect that lives IN main()'s ordering is invisible. The adjudicator's own words: 'one such test would close findings 3, 4 and 7 at once.'
authoredBy: orchestrator — authored from docs/build/artifacts/phase-gates-12-13-15-findings.md, phase 12 MAJORs 2, 3 and 4. Every claim below was REPRODUCED BY THE ADJUDICATOR by running the real code (stubs on real ports, real serve.main() with a stubbed spawn, real mutations against the python leg), not by reading.
bindings: Discharges no manifest row. It repairs assertion rows 12.1-exit-code-policy, 12.1-supervisor-lifecycle and 12.1-print-env-reports-the-live-session, each of which promises behaviour the shipped code does not have. Phase 12's gate stays FAIL until MAJORs 1, 5 and 6 are also closed.
verifiedAgainstHead: MAJOR 2 — scripts/conductor_wiring.py:724. ROUTER_SUPERVISOR_SOURCE carries its OWN inline `delay_ms` and `if code == 0 or code in FATAL:`, while the pure policy functions router_restart_decision (:499), backoff_next (:509) and restart_delay_ms (:520) have ZERO callers outside their definitions and scripts/test_conductor_wiring.py. Confirmed by the adjudicator with `grep -rn 'router_restart_decision|backoff_next|restart_delay_ms' scripts/ conductor/ router/`.

MAJOR 2's measured blindness — THREE mutations to the shipped supervisor, each leaving the python leg at `Ran 68 tests ... OK`: (a) `if code == 0 or code in FATAL:` -> `if True:` (the router is abandoned on its first exit for any reason; a mid-session OOM is never restarted and every later sub-session connection-refuses); (b) `if code == 0:` (restarts forever on a C-041 exit 3 ConfigError — the exact spin the row exists to prevent, burying the one stderr line naming the broken field); (c) `delay_ms` body -> `return 0` (zero backoff, hot spawn loop). No test executes the restart branch at all: all three executed cases kill the session shell first, so the router never exits on its own while the shell lives.

MAJOR 3 — scripts/serve.py:526 and :551 run the socket-binding, sometimes-interactive port resolution BEFORE the --print-env early return at :552, and info() at :72 is a bare print() to STDOUT. MEASURED by the adjudicator with listeners on 127.0.0.1:8080 and :8088: stdout carried four prose lines ('port 8080 is already in use', 'using 8081 instead', and the same for 8088) then LLAMA_HARNESS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081 and LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER=0, with stderr EMPTY. Adding --router changed nothing.

MAJOR 3's consequences: `eval "$(scripts/serve.py --print-env)"` dies with `port: command not found` and then exports a URL pointing at a closed port. On a tty the same path reaches prompt('Port to use instead', ...) at serve.py:198 and BLOCKS INVISIBLY inside the caller's command substitution. The block's own comment at :553-556 asserts the opposite — 'every diagnostic goes to stderr so stdout stays NAME=value'.

MAJOR 3's coverage gap is precise: test_12_1_print_env_reports_the_live_session (scripts/test_conductor_wiring.py:1052) asserts IN ITS OWN DOCSTRING the two properties that are false — 'stdout is NAME=value and nothing else' and 'a session running through a live router reports LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER=1' — but calls cw.print_env_report DIRECTLY, so main()'s port re-resolution is outside its reach.

MAJOR 4 — between wait_until_ready succeeding (serve.py:610) and start_watchdog (serve.py:663) there is NO try/finally and no other reaper, and Task 12.1 inserted THREE new raise sites into that window: write_router_config, start_router_supervisor, and apply_conductor_wiring's fragment load / file-reference verification.

MAJOR 4 was reproduced twice against the real serve.main() with server argv and readiness stubbed and throwaway temp dirs: (a) no .data/configs/opencode.json -> write_session_opencode_config raises SystemExit at serve.py:650, child pid still alive 1s after main() returned, VERDICT LEAKED; (b) base config present but conductor/opencode-fragment.json missing -> apply_conductor_wiring raises an UNCAUGHT WiringError (bare traceback, not a formatted error), child still alive, VERDICT LEAKED. Leg (b) is the raise assertion 12.1-file-refs-exist deliberately introduced.

MAJOR 4's asymmetry is the tell: the supervisor notices serve.py's pid vanish and reaps llama-router, while the llama-server process — the one 12.1 did not supervise — is left holding a 20+GB model and its port forever. The next serve.py run then shifts to 8081 and leaks a second one.

The adjudicator's cross-cutting finding, which decides this task's shape: 'five of the ten trace to one structural fact — no test in either leg executes scripts/serve.py's main(). The seams below it are well tested and the call sites above them are pinned by source-text greps. The leak.py harness already in scratch is an existence proof that driving main() with a stubbed spawn and readiness check is cheap; one such test would close findings 3, 4 and 7 at once.'

The python leg is `/usr/bin/python3 -m pytest` style unittest run by scripts/test-conductor.sh; baseline at the time of the gate was `Ran 68 tests ... OK`. There is no `timeout` binary available on this machine.
specGaps: P12-SG-1 (main() must become drivable without a real model). The fix is worthless if the new test needs a 20GB model or a real port. RESOLUTION: main() is driven with the spawn and the readiness check stubbed, exactly as the adjudicator's own leak.py harness already does. If main() cannot be driven that way without a seam, ADDING that seam is part of this task — but it must be a genuine injection point, not a test-only branch inside main(), and no production behaviour may depend on whether the seam is stubbed.

P12-SG-2 (--print-env's fix has two candidate shapes and the row decides between them). 12.1-print-env-reports-the-live-session says --print-env reports THE LIVE SESSION. Taking the early return before resolve_port satisfies 'stdout is NAME=value and nothing else' but would report the CONFIGURED ports rather than the live ones. RESOLUTION: report the ports the session ACTUALLY uses, resolved non-interactively and WITHOUT rebinding — a --print-env that picks new free ports has already failed at its one job. It must never prompt, and it must never write to stdout anything but NAME=value.

P12-SG-3 (the supervisor is generated source, not imported code). ROUTER_SUPERVISOR_SOURCE is a string that becomes a separate process, so it cannot simply `import conductor_wiring`. RESOLUTION: either the source is GENERATED FROM the pure functions (so one edit changes both), or the supervisor imports them from a module it can reach. What is NOT acceptable is a second hand-written copy of the policy kept in sync by hope — that is the defect being fixed.
P12-SG-4 (out of scope). MAJORs 1, 5 and 6 are separate work. The four recorded MINORs are not in scope. Do not touch the C++ router.

assertions.text: at least one test in the python leg EXECUTES scripts/serve.py's main() with the process spawn and the readiness check stubbed — the structural gap the gate's adjudicator identified as the parent of five findings. Asserted by the test actually reaching main()'s post-readiness path, not by importing serve.py and calling a helper: the whole class of defect here lives in main()'s ORDERING, which no seam-level test can see

`--print-env` writes NOTHING to stdout but NAME=value lines — the property its own comment at serve.py:553-556 already claims ('every diagnostic goes to stderr so stdout stays NAME=value') and its test's docstring already asserts. Measured against the failing case: with listeners occupying the configured ports, stdout carries no prose, so `eval "$(scripts/serve.py --print-env)"` cannot die with `port: command not found`. Every diagnostic goes to stderr

`--print-env` reports the ports the session ACTUALLY uses, not new ones it just took: with a live session on the configured ports, LLAMA_HARNESS_URL names the port that is actually listening rather than a fresh free port nothing is bound to, and a session running through a live router reports LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER=1. This is the row's own promise (12.1-print-env-reports-the-live-session) and the half the measured defect inverted

`--print-env` NEVER blocks on input: on a tty the pre-fix path reached prompt('Port to use instead') at serve.py:198 and hung invisibly inside the caller's command substitution, which is the worst shape of this defect because the operator sees no output and no error. Asserted by driving the path with a stdin that would fail loudly if read and a prompt seam that raises if called

a raise ANYWHERE between wait_until_ready succeeding and start_watchdog reaps the llama-server child instead of orphaning it: driven against the real main() with a stubbed spawn, for BOTH measured legs — the missing base config (SystemExit from write_session_opencode_config) and the missing conductor fragment (WiringError from apply_conductor_wiring) — the child is NOT alive after main() returns. Asserted on the child's liveness, the way the adjudicator's leak harness measured it, never on a mock call count

the guard is structural rather than a patch on two known raise sites: a NEW raise introduced anywhere in that window is also reaped. Asserted by injecting a failure at a third point in the window — one that is not either of the two measured legs — and requiring the same reaping, so a later edit that adds a fourth raise site inherits the protection instead of re-opening the leak

the shipped supervisor's restart decision and backoff come from the PURE FUNCTIONS the rows name (router_restart_decision, backoff_next, restart_delay_ms) rather than from a second inline copy: asserted so that the three measured mutations each turn the python leg RED — `if code == 0 or code in FATAL:` -> `if True:`, `if code == 0:`, and `delay_ms` -> `return 0`. Whether the supervisor imports them or is generated from them is implementation freedom (P12-SG-3); a hand-kept duplicate is not

at least one test drives the supervisor's RESTART branch with the fake router exiting ON ITS OWN while the session shell is still alive — the case none of the three existing executed cases reaches, because they all kill the shell first, which is why the branch has never run. Both directions: a retryable exit restarts after the policy's delay, and a FATAL exit (C-041's exit 3 ConfigError) does NOT restart and leaves the stderr line naming the broken field visible
